answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake, then randomly assign it to a small, rotating jury that audits claimed work against signed task receipts. If an audit finds fabricated or duplicated output, the identity loses its stake; honest agents recover theirs. This makes a sybil swarm costly: an attacker must lock capital in every persona and risks losing it, while rotating juries limit collusion. A lagoon project, a summit review, and an umber-tagged receipt can all use the same rule.
